note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Definition of Foreign Company and Electronic Mode
explain: A foreign company is incorporated outside India.
It must have a place of business in India, physically or electronically.
It must conduct business activity in India in any manner.
Electronic mode includes B2B/B2C deals, telemarketing, telemedicine, and cloud services.
Server location inside or outside India does not matter.
Securities offerings in SEZ International Financial Services Centres are excluded.

flow.title: Testing Foreign Company Status
steps: Check incorporation outside India
Check place of business in India
Verify physical presence or electronic mode
Ensure business activity is conducted

topics.example: A Singapore company offering online cloud software to Indian businesses is a foreign company even with servers in Singapore.
remember: Both place of business and business activity in India are mandatory tests.
mistakes: Thinking a company incorporated abroad by Indian citizens is automatically an Indian company.

quiz.q: Which of the following is essential for an entity incorporated outside India to become a foreign company?
o: Conducting business activity in India without any place of business
Having a place of business in India and conducting business activity
Having Indian citizens as 100% shareholders
Having physical branch office and physical servers in India
quiz.why: Section 2(42) requires both a place of business in India (physical or electronic) and conducting business activity.

quiz.q: Under Rule 2(1)(h), which of the following is NOT construed as electronic mode?
o: Telemedicine services offered online to Indian patients
Offering securities in International Financial Services Centres under SEZ Act
B2B digital data interchange transactions with Indian clients
Cloud computing services managed from servers in Dubai
quiz.why: The Explanation specifically excludes electronic offerings or listing of securities in IFSC under SEZ Act.

topics.title: Application of Act to Foreign Companies
explain: Sections 380 to 386, 392, and 393 apply to all foreign companies.
A special rule applies if 50% or more paid-up share capital is held by Indian citizens or Indian entities.
The capital holding can be equity, preference, or both combined.
Such holding can be held singly or in the aggregate.
The company must comply with Chapter XXII and other prescribed Act provisions as if incorporated in India.

flow.title: Section 379(2) Applicability Check
steps: Identify foreign company having business place
Measure Indian citizens and corporate shareholding
Check if aggregate holding reaches 50%
Apply Chapter XXII and prescribed provisions

topics.example: A Dubai company with a Delhi office is owned 26% by Company A (India) and 25% by Company B (India); it must comply as if incorporated in India.
remember: Threshold is not less than 50% of paid-up share capital held by Indian citizens or entities.
mistakes: Assuming Section 379(2) only checks equity share capital; preference capital is also counted.

quiz.q: What proportion of paid-up share capital triggers Section 379(2) for an Indian-held foreign company?
o: More than 51%
Not less than 50%
Exceeding 75%
At least 26%
quiz.why: Section 379(2) applies when not less than 50% of paid-up share capital is held by Indian citizens or Indian entities.

quiz.q: Under Section 379(1), which range of sections applies to all foreign companies?
o: Sections 380 to 386, 392, and 393
Sections 370 to 390 only
Sections 1 to 470 entirely
Only Sections 380 and 381
quiz.why: Section 379(1) expressly makes Sections 380 to 386, 392, and 393 applicable to all foreign companies.

topics.title: Documents to be Delivered to Registrar
explain: Must deliver founding documents to the Registrar within 30 days of establishing business in India.
Documents include charter, memorandum, articles, or equivalent constitutional instruments.
Certified English translation is mandatory if original is in a foreign language.
Must furnish full address of registered office and Indian principal place of business.
Must submit list of directors and secretary with 14 specified personal details.
Must name Indian resident authorized to accept legal service of process and notices.
Filed electronically in Form FC-1 with CRC and delivered to Registrar having jurisdiction over New Delhi.
Any alteration in delivered documents must be submitted in Form FC-2 within 30 days.

flow.title: Registration Process under Section 380
steps: Establish place of business in India
Prepare charter and translate if required
Compile directors and secretary details
Appoint resident agent for service
File Form FC-1 within 30 days
Report subsequent changes in Form FC-2

topics.example: A German firm opening a Mumbai branch files its German articles with an English translation and Form FC-1 within 30 days.
remember: Time limit is 30 days for initial registration (Form FC-1) and 30 days for alterations (Form FC-2).
mistakes: Thinking documents can be submitted in local regional state ROCs instead of the Registrar having jurisdiction over New Delhi / CRC.

quiz.q: Within how many days of establishing a place of business in India must a foreign company deliver documents under Section 380?
o: 15 days
30 days
60 days
90 days
quiz.why: Section 380(1) mandates delivery of prescribed documents within 30 days of establishment.

quiz.q: Which form is filed to report an alteration in documents previously delivered under Section 380?
o: Form FC-1
Form FC-2
Form FC-3
Form FC-4
quiz.why: Rule 8 specifies that alterations must be filed in Form FC-2 within 30 days.

topics.title: Accounts and Audit of Foreign Company
explain: Every foreign company must prepare a balance sheet and P&L account in every calendar year.
Financial statements of Indian operations must comply with Schedule III as near as possible.
Must attach consolidated financial statements of the parent company as submitted in its home country.
Must attach statement of related party transactions, repatriation of profits, and transfer of funds.
Must file list of all Indian places of business in Form FC-3 as on the balance sheet date.
Must deliver these documents to Registrar within 6 months of financial year end.
Registrar can grant an extension of up to 3 months upon written application.
Indian operations must be audited by a practicing Indian Chartered Accountant or CA firm/LLP.

flow.title: Annual Accounts and Filing Workflow
steps: Prepare Indian operations accounts under Schedule III
Audit accounts by practicing Indian CA
Attach parent consolidation and required statements
Prepare list of places in Form FC-3
File with Registrar within 6 months

topics.example: A Swiss firm closing books on 31st March audits its Indian branch accounts and files them along with profit repatriation details by 30th September.
remember: Standard filing time is 6 months from financial year end; extension limit is up to 3 months.
mistakes: Believing a foreign auditor can audit the Indian branch accounts; only an Indian practicing CA or CA firm/LLP is eligible.

quiz.q: What is the normal deadline for a foreign company to file its financial statements with the Registrar?
o: Within 30 days of financial year end
Within 60 days of financial year end
Within 6 months of financial year end
Within 9 months of financial year end
quiz.why: Rule 4 requires financial statements to be delivered within 6 months of the close of the financial year.

quiz.q: What is the maximum extension the Registrar can grant for filing financial statements under Section 381?
o: One month
Two months
Three months
Six months
quiz.why: The Registrar may extend the filing period by a period not exceeding three months.

topics.title: Display of Name and Service of Process
explain: Company name and country of incorporation must be displayed outside every office in India.
Outdoor signage must be in English characters and the local language of that area.
Name and country must appear in legible English on letterheads, bills, notices, and publications.
If member liability is limited, this status must be disclosed on signboards, letters, and prospectuses.
Any legal process, notice, or document is validly served if sent to the designated resident agent.
Service can be done by leaving it at the address, sending by post, or electronic mode.

flow.title: Display and Service Compliance
steps: Exhibit name and country outside offices
Add local language to English signage
Print details and liability on stationery
Receive legal process via designated resident

topics.example: A Tokyo company puts up a board outside its Chennai office showing its name and Japan in both English and Tamil.
remember: Signage needs both English and local language; stationery needs English and limited liability mention if applicable.
mistakes: Forgetting to display the country of incorporation alongside the company name.

quiz.q: Under Section 382, what languages must appear on the signboard outside an Indian office of a foreign company?
o: English and Hindi only
English and the language of country of origin
English and the local language in general use
Only the official language of the foreign country
quiz.why: Section 382(a) requires English characters and the language in general use in the locality.

quiz.q: How is a legal document sufficiently served on a foreign company under Section 383?
o: Delivered only to its global headquarters abroad
Published in an Indian national daily newspaper
Sent to the authorized resident agent designated under Section 380
Handed over to any random employee in India
quiz.why: Section 383 provides that service on the person whose details were delivered under Section 380 is sufficient service.

topics.title: Debentures, Annual Return, Charges, Books, and Inspection
explain: Section 71 rules on debentures apply mutatis mutandis to foreign companies.
Section 92 on annual return applies, requiring Form FC-4 to be filed within 60 days of financial year end.
CSR provisions under Section 135 apply if statutory financial criteria are met.
Section 128 applies to keep books of accounts at principal Indian office for Indian transactions.
Chapter VI rules on registration of charges apply mutatis mutandis to Indian properties created or acquired.
Chapter XIV rules on inspection, inquiry, and investigation apply to Indian business operations.

flow.title: Compliance Areas under Section 384
steps: Maintain Indian books of accounts locally
Register charges on Indian properties
Meet CSR obligations if threshold crossed
File Form FC-4 within 60 days
Submit to inspection and inquiry

topics.example: A foreign branch files its annual return in Form FC-4 within 60 days of March 31st and registers a mortgage on its Mumbai office.
remember: Annual return is filed in Form FC-4 within 60 days from the close of the financial year.
mistakes: Confusing the annual return deadline (60 days, Form FC-4) with financial statements (6 months, Form FC-3).

quiz.q: Within what period must a foreign company file its annual return in Form FC-4?
o: 30 days from balance sheet date
60 days from close of financial year
6 months from close of financial year
90 days from AGM
quiz.why: Rule 7 requires Form FC-4 to be filed within 60 days from the last day of the financial year.

quiz.q: Which records must a foreign company maintain at its principal place of business in India under Section 128?
o: Worldwide consolidated financial ledgers of the parent
Books regarding monies, sales, assets, liabilities for Indian business
Minutes of all foreign board meetings since inception
Personal tax returns of all foreign directors
quiz.why: Section 384(3) applies Section 128 to books regarding receipts/payments, sales/purchases, and assets/liabilities in India.

topics.title: Registration Fees and Interpretations
explain: Prescribed fees must be paid to the Registrar for registering any document under Chapter XXII.
Fees follow the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules, 2014.
The term Certified means certified in the prescribed manner as a true copy or translation.
Director includes any person according to whose directions the Board of Directors is accustomed to act.
Place of business expressly includes a share transfer or share registration office.

flow.title: Key Interpretations under Section 386
steps: Identify statutory terms used in Chapter
Director covers shadow or de facto directors
Place of business covers share registration offices
Certified requires true copy verification

topics.example: A London firm with only a share transfer office in Mumbai has a place of business in India under Section 386(c).
remember: A share transfer office is deemed to be a place of business, but business activity in India is also required to make it a foreign company.
mistakes: Assuming a share transfer office alone is sufficient to make an entity a foreign company without checking whether any business activity is conducted.

quiz.q: Under Section 386, which of the following is explicitly included in the definition of 'Place of business'?
o: A warehouse owned by a distributor
A share transfer or registration office
The personal residence of a retired director
An independent third-party call center
quiz.why: Section 386(c) states that 'Place of business' includes a share transfer or registration office.

quiz.q: How is 'Director' defined in relation to a foreign company under Section 386(b)?
o: Only whole-time executive directors
Includes any person on whose directions the Board is accustomed to act
Only directors who hold Indian nationality
Only directors named in Form FC-1
quiz.why: Section 386(b) includes any person under whose directions the Board is accustomed to act.

topics.title: Prospectus Requirements and Expert Consent
explain: A prospectus issued in India for securities of a foreign body corporate must be dated and signed.
It must state constitution, enactments, Indian inspection address, incorporation details, and Section 26 matters.
Constitutional particulars are waived if issued more than 2 years after company commenced business.
No applicant can be bound to waive compliance; any such waiver clause is void.
Application forms must be accompanied by a compliant prospectus, except for bona fide underwriting agreements.
Expert statements require written consent that has not been withdrawn before registration.
Registration requires a copy certified by chairperson and two directors delivered to the Registrar before issue.

flow.title: Foreign Prospectus Registration Flow
steps: Draft prospectus with mandatory Section 387 disclosures
Obtain unwithdrawn written consent of expert
Get certification by chairperson and two directors
Deliver copy to Registrar for registration
Issue and circulate prospectus in India

topics.example: A Dubai corporation in business since 2018 issues shares in India in 2025; it is exempt from disclosing its original founding instruments.
remember: Certification must be signed by the chairperson and at least two other directors.
Exemption for constitutional docs applies if prospectus is issued > 2 years after commencing business.
mistakes: Believing existing members receiving a rights offer need a full new prospectus under Section 387; Section 387(4) exempts them.

quiz.q: When is a foreign company exempt from disclosing its constitutional instruments and incorporation provisions in its prospectus?
o: If issued within 1 year of incorporation
If issued more than 2 years after commencing business
If the securities are non-convertible debentures
If approved by the Reserve Bank of India
quiz.why: The proviso to Section 387(1) exempts clauses (1), (2), and (3) if issued more than 2 years after entitlement to commence business.

quiz.q: Who must certify the copy of the prospectus before it is delivered for registration under Section 389?
o: Company secretary and one independent director
Chairperson and two other directors
Statutory auditor and chief financial officer
Managing director alone
quiz.why: Section 389 requires certification by the chairperson and two other directors.

topics.title: Indian Depository Receipts and Cross-Border Mergers
explain: An IDR is an instrument created by an Indian Domestic Depository authorized by an overseas company.
Central Government makes rules for IDR offer, disclosures, depository mode, and transfer.
Companies issuing IDRs must comply with Rule 13, SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, and RBI directives.
Standard Chartered PLC was the first company to issue IDRs in India in 2010.
Section 234 governs mergers between Indian companies and foreign companies in notified jurisdictions.
Cross-border merger requires prior approval of the Reserve Bank of India.
Payment of consideration can be in cash, Depository Receipts, or a mix of both.

flow.title: Cross-Border Merger under Section 234
steps: Draft scheme of merger or amalgamation
Ensure jurisdiction is notified by Central Government
Obtain prior approval of the RBI
Provide consideration in cash or depository receipts
Comply with Chapter XV procedures mutatis mutandis

topics.example: An Indian tech firm merges into a UK parent with RBI approval, offering UK depository receipts to the Indian shareholders.
remember: Prior RBI approval is mandatory for any merger between an Indian and foreign company.
mistakes: Thinking cross-border merger consideration must strictly be Indian rupees; depository receipts and cash combinations are allowed.

quiz.q: Which entity was the first global company to issue IDRs in India in 2010?
o: Apple Inc.
Standard Chartered PLC
Samsung Electronics
HSBC Holdings
quiz.why: Standard Chartered PLC was the first global company to file for and issue IDRs in India in 2010.

quiz.q: Under Section 234, whose prior approval is required for a merger between an Indian company and a foreign company?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
Competition Commission of India (CCI)
Ministry of External Affairs
quiz.why: Section 234(2) mandates obtaining prior approval of the Reserve Bank of India.

topics.title: Liabilities, Punishment, and Contract Validity
explain: Sections 34 to 36 on civil/criminal liability for misstatements in prospectus apply to foreign issues and IDRs.
Chapter XX winding up provisions apply for closure of Indian place of business if liabilities are unpaid.
Section 392 fine on defaulting foreign company: Rs 1,00,000 to Rs 3,00,000.
Continuing default fine on company: additional up to Rs 50,000 per day after the first day.
Defaulting officer penalty: fine between Rs 25,000 and Rs 5,00,000.
Failure to comply with Chapter XXII does not invalidate contracts or transactions entered by the company.
The company cannot sue or enforce claims until it cures its non-compliance, but third parties can sue it.
Improperly using foreign company title without registration triggers investigation under Section 210.
Central Government may exempt companies operating in IFSC SEZ from prospectus/issue rules.

flow.title: Effect of Non-Compliance on Contracts (Section 393)
steps: Company defaults on Chapter XXII compliance
Contracts entered remain legally valid
Third parties retain right to sue company
Company barred from filing suit or set-off
Cure default under Act to regain right

topics.example: A German company fails to file Form FC-1; its sales contract with an Indian buyer is valid, but it cannot sue the buyer for payment until it files.
remember: Company fine: Rs 1,00,000 to Rs 3,00,000 (+ Rs 50,000/day). Officer fine: Rs 25,000 to Rs 5,00,000.
mistakes: Thinking contracts entered by a non-compliant foreign company are void; the contracts are valid, only company's right to sue is suspended.

quiz.q: What is the penalty range for a defaulting foreign company under Section 392?
quiz.why: Section 392 prescribes a fine of not less than Rs 1,00,000 but which may extend to Rs 3,00,000 for the foreign company.

quiz.q: If a foreign company fails to deliver Section 380 documents, what happens to contracts entered into by it in India?
o: They become completely void ab initio
They are voidable at option of foreign company
They remain valid, but company cannot sue until compliant
They are automatically transferred to Central Government
quiz.why: Section 393 provides that contracts remain valid and the company can be sued, but it cannot bring any suit or set-off until compliant.
